newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee heads lower as NY takes a correction.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee heads lower as NY takes a correction.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures raked up further losses in quiet Wednesday afternoon dealings as New York embarked on a downward correction to recent sharp rises, traders said.
Dealings were relatively thin and Truxo was a featured seller in the afternoon.
Most active May tumbled from a high of $1,558 a tonne to end at the day's low of $1,528 for a $30 loss while other months were $5 to $26 down.
Traders said New York's sharp correction came a day after front-month March hit a peak of 150.50 cents a lb on Tuesday.
"I think some of the hunger (for higher prices) has gone out of the market," said one.
"The time is right for a correction," he added. By London's close, New York had retraced about five cents and traders said further losses were possible.
Traders said business had dwindled in London after hectic fund-backed trading volumes in the past weeks.
Since then, there has been a dearth of both origin and roaster participation. Traders said prices should pull back further to attract fresh industry involvement.
"The coffee trade needs the market lower to get the physical business on the go again," the same trader said.
"We are not seeing any great origin activity up here...the roasters are nibbling, they are not fixing their big stuff yet." Manufacturers are likely to wait for much lower values to fix their prices.
In other news, robusta producers have called off a meeting in Bali, Indonesia due on Thursday after an Ivorian minister failed to make the trip.
The producers met informally on Tuesday night but no decision was made on the sharing of export quotas agreed recently at a meeting in Brazil.
At the Brazilian meeting, producers agreed to cut robusta exports by a further one million bags and arabica exports by 300,000 bags.
Traders, sceptical of any new producer effort to limit supplies, said the cancellation of the Bali meeting came as no surprise to them. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
